units.source_text: 有一次，先生招待我喝酒，当时夫人也在座，还为我们斟酒。

en.t: Once, Sensei invited me to drink with him; his wife was there too, and poured sake for us.

units.source_text: 先生好像比平时都高兴，对夫人说：“你也喝一杯吧。”

en.t: Sensei seemed happier than usual, and said to his wife, “You have a cup too.”

units.source_text: 并把自己喝干的酒盅递了过去。

en.t: Then he handed her the cup he had just emptied.

units.source_text: “我……”夫人本想推辞，但还是勉为其难地接过了酒盅。

en.t: “I...” His wife began to refuse, but reluctantly took the cup after all.

units.source_text: 她蹙起漂亮的眉头，抿了一口我给她斟的半杯酒。

en.t: She knit her beautiful brows and took a sip from the half cup of sake I had poured for her.

units.source_text: 之后，夫人和先生开始了下面这番对话：

en.t: After that, his wife and Sensei began the following exchange:

units.source_text: “真是稀罕哪，你平时可是很少让我喝酒的啊！”

en.t: “How unusual. You almost never let me drink.”

units.source_text: “因为你不喜欢喝酒嘛。

en.t: “Because you do not like drinking.

units.source_text: 不过，偶尔喝一杯挺好，能够使人心情愉快。”

en.t: Still, it is good to have a cup now and then; it can make a person cheerful.”

units.source_text: “一点儿没觉得愉快啊，只觉得辣。

en.t: “It does not make me cheerful at all. It only tastes harsh.

units.source_text: 不过，看你的样子只要一喝酒就很高兴。”

en.t: But from the look of you, you become very happy whenever you drink.”

units.source_text: “有时候很高兴，但不是每次都能这样。”

en.t: “Sometimes I do become very happy, but it is not like that every time.”

units.source_text: “今晚怎么样？”

en.t: “How about tonight?”

units.source_text: “今天很愉快呀。”

en.t: “Tonight I feel quite good.”

units.source_text: “以后每天晚上都喝一点儿嘛。”

en.t: “Then have a little every night from now on.”

units.source_text: “那可不行。”

en.t: “That would not do.”

units.source_text: “还是喝一点儿吧，那样就不会觉得寂寞了。”

en.t: “Please do have a little. Then you will not feel so lonely.”

units.source_text: 先生家里只有夫妇俩和一个女佣，

en.t: There were only Sensei, his wife, and one maid in Sensei's household,

units.source_text: 我每次去，房间里都静悄悄的，从没听见过高声谈笑，

en.t: and whenever I went there, the house was quiet; I never heard loud talk or laughter,

units.source_text: 以至有时我觉得屋子里仿佛只有先生和我两个人似的。

en.t: so that at times I felt as if Sensei and I were the only two people in the house.

units.source_text: “要是有个孩子就好啦。”

en.t: “It would be nice if we had a child.”

units.source_text: 夫人对我说。

en.t: His wife said this to me.

units.source_text: “是啊。”我虽然这样回答，可心里并没有产生任何共鸣。

en.t: “Yes, it would,” I answered, but I felt no real sympathy in my heart.

units.source_text: 那时我还没有结婚生子，只觉得小孩子很烦人。

en.t: At that time I was not married and had no children, and I only thought of children as troublesome.

units.source_text: “要一个来给你，怎么样？”

en.t: “Shall we get one for you?”

units.source_text: 先生说。

en.t: Sensei said.
